AI Agents on "Low-End" Hardware [2/3]

A local AI agent inspecting a Linux system, troubleshooting shell commands and analyzing installed software. Running on a nearly 16-year-old CPU and a GPU with just 4GB of VRAM.

Hardware:
Core i5-650
8GB DDR3 RAM
AMD Radeon RX 570 4GB

Model: Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M
Backend: llama.cpp (Vulkan)
Agent: OpenCode with shell access

The task: Find out which installed Flatpak application occupies the most disk space on the system.

The result? The agent explored the available Flatpak commands, consulted the help output, experimented with different command options, and eventually combined Flatpak, awk and sort to analyze the installed applications.

Element came out on top with 546.2 MB, followed by Bottles with 529.3 MB and ghostwriter with 470 MB.

Total runtime: 5 minutes and 16 seconds.

The interesting part wasn't just finding the largest application. The agent initially struggled with incorrect command syntax and unavailable columns, but adapted its approach by consulting the documentation and testing alternative commands.

This is another example of a small model using real system tools to solve a practical Linux administration task.

Many AI agent guides recommend 16GB of RAM or more as a starting point. But do you really need that much for every use case?

My experiments suggest otherwise. With a small quantized model and an efficient backend, even 8GB of system RAM can be enough for surprisingly useful agent workflows.

No cloud. No expensive hardware.

Just a nearly 15-year-old PC showing what is already possible.
